newsitem.title: FRANCE: French franc slips on vote, testing 3.3850 vs mark.
newsitem.headline: French franc slips on vote, testing 3.3850 vs mark.

text.p: The French franc extended Sunday's losses in early Monday trading, falling to its lowest level this year, after the Socialist-led left swept to power in a parliamentary election.
It touched a low of 3.3860 against the mark and was testing the 3.3850 level, seen by traders as a key support level. It was trading at 3.3848 at 0615 GMT.
A trader at a French bank said, the mark "rose a little bit (against the franc) this morning. There is liquidity but not but not much volitility".
He said it was "difficult to say" whether the franc was being supported by the Bank of France. "I don't see anything at the moment."
Traders in Tokyo and Singapore said the franc's decline had been cushioned by talk of intervention by the French central bank, adding liquidity and taking the sting out of the drop.
Analysts said some investors had a target of 3.40 per mark in place in the case of a combined Socialist-Communist victory in the election.

French call money, a semi-official interest rate closely steered by the Bank of France was unchanged at 3-1/8 1/4 percent. Money market traders said there was slight pressure on the overnight rate, trading at near the top of its range, but nothing serious.
Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro Finance, said he still expected the franc to come under further pressure.
"I would still see more downside for the franc and fixed income markets relative to Germany. He said he expected 3.3950 per mark support to be tested.

Another trader at a French bank in Paris said 3.3850 was clearly a level which was attracting a lot of interest from both buyers and sellers while French bond and interest rate futures were holding relatively well.
"That said, if there is a crisis, it could come in several stages," he said.

"We have to see how the large U.S. funds react to the presence of the Communists in the government in 1997 and how the Socialists succeed in reconciling their European commitments with measures such as the reduction of working hours or the creation of jobs in the public sector," he said.
He said 3.3825 per mark looked set to be the likely high for the franc and if it were to weaken it could drop to 3.3950-3.4000 without much panic.

"You have to especially watch the peripherals such as the mark/lira and the mark/peseta, which are more free than the mark/franc. If they're under pressure as well, the mark/franc can only adjust through the franc/peseta and the franc/lira," he said.
